faqs.question: What is the difference between standard and automotive IGBT modules?
faqs.answer: Automotive IGBT modules undergo additional qualification testing per AEC-Q101 standards, including extended temperature cycling, vibration testing, and higher reliability requirements. They also feature enhanced quality tracking and traceability required for automotive applications. Standard modules are cost-optimized for industrial applications with slightly relaxed qualification requirements.
faqs.decisionGuide: Choose automotive modules for EV applications; standard modules for industrial drives.

faqs.question: How do I calculate losses in CRRC IGBT modules?
faqs.answer: IGBT module losses consist of conduction losses and switching losses. conduction loss = Ic × Vce(sat) × duty cycle. Switching loss = (Eon + Eoff) × switching frequency. cRRC provides detailed loss curves in datasheets. For accurate estimation, use the switching energy values at your operating current and temperature, then multiply by switching frequency. Total losses determine heatsink requirements.
faqs.decisionGuide: Use our loss calculator tool or contact FAE for detailed thermal analysis.

faqs.question: What is the typical gate drive voltage for CRRC IGBT modules?
faqs.answer: CRRC IGBT modules are typically driven with +15V for turn-on and -8V to -15V for turn-off. The negative turn-off voltage improves noise immunity and prevents false triggering. Gate drive circuits should provide peak currents of 2-10A depending on module size for fast switching. CRRC recommends using their specified gate resistor values for optimal performance.
faqs.decisionGuide: Follow datasheet recommendations or contact FAE for gate drive design assistance.

faqs.question: What protection features are built into CRRC IGBT modules?
faqs.answer: CRRC IGBT modules include multiple protection features: (1) Short-circuit withstand capability (typically 10μs), (2) Overtemperature sensing via NTC thermistor, (3) Overcurrent protection through desaturation detection, (4) Active clamping for overvoltage protection. External protection circuits should be implemented in the gate driver for complete system protection.
faqs.decisionGuide: Implement all recommended protection circuits for reliable operation.

faqs.question: Can CRRC IGBT modules be used in parallel?
faqs.answer: Yes, CRRC IGBT modules can be paralleled for higher current capacity. Key considerations include: (1) Modules from same production lot for matched characteristics, (2) Symmetrical layout with equal stray inductance, (3) Individual gate resistors for each module, (4) Common collector and emitter connections at module terminals, (5) Current derating (typically 10-15%) to account for imbalance. Proper design verification is essential.
faqs.decisionGuide: Contact our FAE for parallel operation design review and recommendations.
